answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock.. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. Consider a wharf as the anchor of the cost.
